newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Primedia up, Interleisure buy worries wane.
newsitem.headline: Primedia up, Interleisure buy worries wane.

text.p: Shares in Primedia Ltd bounced on Monday, recovering from recent lows which were prompted by market views that the media firm is set to pay a big premium for a stake in cinema group Interleisure Ltd.
Dealers and analysts said that the downside on the shares had been overdone especially as Primedia was poised to become involved in other new, and potentially lucrative, ventures.

"(News) that they've upped their bid for Interleisure has been around on the market for a while and I think initially it was perceived last week that perhaps they could be overpaying," said James Scott of Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.

"There's been a little bit of a retracement this morning...I think they've got a couple of other things on the go as well, including a television station, which could settle the price a little bit and even firm it up," he said.
By about 1225 GMT Primedia shares were up 170 cents or 5.99 percent to 30.10 rand. The group's "N" shares added 150 cents to 26.90 rand.

Reports last week said that Primedia had reached agreement in principle to set up a consortium with the state-owned South African Broadcasting Corporation to bid for a new private sector commercial television channel.

Business Times newspaper on Sunday quoted sources as saying that Primedia had upped its offer for the 44.3 percent stake in Interleisure to 1.7 billion rand. Speculation pegged the initial offer at 1.4 billion rand.
Primedia looks fairly certain to bag Interleisure following a cautionary from the firm on Friday saying that an announcement on a "material acquisition" was anticipated shortly.
A media analyst said that Primedia was likely to issue shares or use its existing cash reserves to fund the buy.

The other main contender for the Interleisure stake, film equipment and advertising firm Sasani Ltd, seems unlikely to secure it after chairman Nic Frangos said last week it would not overburden itself if the price tag was too high.

Primedia's ordinary and "N" shares have fallen around 20 percent since early June amid a barrage of rumours on the Interleisure bid. Sasani's stock was also hard-hit at the end of June and early July when it lost over 30 percent of its value.
The sale of Interleisure, which holds a 20 percent stake in Sasani, is part of the unbundling of Servgro International which together with Kersaf Ltd jointly own Interleisure.
Servgro's share price was last up 30 cents at 930 cents.
